evals.prompt: Make an animated diagram for our README showing how a GET /users/:id request hits the API, checks Redis, and falls back to Postgres on a miss.
evals.expected_output: An animated SVG committed under docs/ or similar, with cache-hit and cache-miss steps.
expectations: Produces an .svg with scripts/svg.mjs, not hand-written SVG
Has two steps, one for cache hit and one for cache miss
Redis and Postgres use shape store
The reply to the browser replays the request edge with back: true instead of adding a return edge
Cards show concrete data such as a user id and a name
scripts/lint.mjs reports no layout warnings for the spec

evals.prompt: Explain the OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE to a new engineer. Something interactive I can open in a browser.
evals.expected_output: An interactive HTML page with authorize, token exchange, and refresh steps.
expectations: Produces a self-contained .html with scripts/html.mjs
Shows the code verifier staying on the client and only its hash being sent
Has separate steps for authorization and token exchange
Every beat has a one-sentence say
No layout warnings

evals.prompt: Here's our deploy pipeline in Mermaid. Turn it into something animated we can post in Slack.
evals.expected_output: An MP4 or GIF made from the Mermaid source.
expectations: Uses scripts/from-mermaid.mjs to create the spec
Exports with scripts/video.mjs to .mp4 or .gif
The yes and no branches of the test decision become separate steps
The registry is drawn as a store

evals.prompt: This trace export shows a slow checkout. Animate it so the team can see where the time goes.
evals.expected_output: A diagram generated from the trace, showing per-call durations.
expectations: Uses scripts/from-otel.mjs on the trace file
The slow external payment call and its duration are visible in a card or caption
The failing trace appears as its own step with the error shown
Databases and the Kafka topic are drawn as stores

evals.prompt: Add a diagram to this PR description that shows what changes: requests now go through a rate limiter before the API.
evals.expected_output: An animated SVG with before and after steps or a limited/allowed pair of steps.
expectations: The rate limiter is a box between the client and the API, with edges only between neighbours
Has a step where a request is rejected with 429
Output is an SVG suitable for a PR description
No layout warnings
